items.title: The model inside the server: Network design for inference on a few GPU nodes
items.summary_1line: Explains network design for inference on a few GPU nodes, using a 4-server, 8-GPU example running Llama 3.3 70B with vLLM, and argues that request handling and session count matter more than GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.
items.editor_note: 자체 호스팅 쪽 사례를 더한다. 70B 모델을 GPU 서버 4대에서 돌릴 때 병목이 어디에 생기는지 다룬다.

editorial.tldr: This is a loose topic cluster about running inference on GPUs, not one event. Its main thread is AWS adding managed ways to share one GPU: NVIDIA MIG partitions for SageMaker endpoints on Nov 6, then Lambda GPU functions with up to 48 concurrent invocations per model on Nov 22.
editorial.whats_new: An APNIC design guide for self-hosted inference on a few GPU nodes, built on a 4-server, 8-GPU vLLM setup running Llama 3.3 70B, argues that request handling and session count matter more than GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.
editorial.why_it_matters: Whether you rent shared GPUs from AWS or run a few nodes yourself, utilization now depends on how requests are batched and routed more than on raw interconnect speed.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before buying faster interconnect for a small self-hosted cluster, load-test request concurrency and session counts on vLLM; for bursty small models, benchmark SageMaker MIG and Lambda GPU first.
